s: Kakatiyas were subordinates of which dynasty in Andhra
x:
The early Kakatiyas served as feudatories of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi before emerging as an independent power. The earliest Kakatiya chiefs such as Beta I and Prola I acknowledged the overlordship of the Eastern Chalukya rulers. As the power of the Eastern Chalukyas declined, the Kakatiyas gradually strengthened their position and eventually established an independent kingdom under Rudradeva with Warangal (Orugallu) as their capital.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).

s: Who gets the credit for keeping Telugu in History of Andhra?
x:
The Renati Cholas occupy a unique place in the history of Telugu because they were the first rulers to use Telugu as the language of official inscriptions. Their inscriptions, dating from the 6th century CE, mark the earliest known use of Telugu for administrative purposes. Before this period, inscriptions in Andhra were predominantly written in Prakrit or Sanskrit. The famous Kalamalla Inscription of Erikal Mutturaju Dhananjaya, a Renati Chola ruler, is regarded as the earliest complete inscription in Telugu.
Thus, the Renati Cholas are credited with giving Telugu official recognition in administration and epigraphy.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).

s: Which is the oldest basin in Andhra Pradesh?
x:
The Kadapa Basin (Cuddapah Basin) is the oldest geological basin in Andhra Pradesh and one of the oldest sedimentary basins in India. It was formed during the Proterozoic Era, approximately 1.6 billion years ago, and consists of thick sequences of sedimentary and metamorphic rocks. The basin occupies large parts of YSR Kadapa, Nandyal, Kurnool, Annamayya and Prakasam districts. The Kadapa Basin is economically important because it contains rich deposits of limestone, barytes, asbestos, dolomite, quartz and uranium. The famous Mangampeta Barytes Mine, one of the largest barytes deposits in the world, is located within this basin.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).
